category_title: Students with low self-confidence and difficulty with spatial-fractional concepts
student_description: Avery is a student with severe math anxiety who hyper-focuses on performance and struggles with spatial organization and standard fraction diagrams, often misidentifying denominators based on remaining parts. She uniquely needs math to be reframed through her interests in design and patterns, using concrete manipulables and open-ended construction tasks to shift her focus from getting the 'right answer' to mastering the process.

criteria.rationale: Avery is triggered by standard visual diagrams of fractions but thrives when spatial tasks are grounded in concrete, manipulable parts.
criteria.check: The tutor introduces or frames the fraction task using concrete, manipulable objects or design components (e.g., pre-cut shapes, quilt pieces) rather than abstract 2D diagrams.

criteria.rationale: Because Avery struggles with spatial organization and often misidentifies denominators based on remaining parts, she needs explicit help relating smaller pieces to the whole.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly guides the student to classify or relate individual parts or shapes to their specific fractional proportion of the whole.

criteria.rationale: Avery hyper-focuses on getting the right answer and panics; giving her a concrete process to check her own work shifts her focus to mastery in the moment.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts the student to verify her own work using a specific mathematical process (such as converting to a common denominator to see if parts add up to a whole) rather than simply confirming if an answer is right or wrong.
